changes.description: Public POJO in package com.neversoft.customer following the Vehicle.java style. Private fields id (long), name, email, phone (String). No-arg and all-fields constructors, getter/setter per field, equals/hashCode/toString using java.util.Objects. No reference to orders.

Public child POJO in package com.neversoft.sales. Private fields id (long), itemCode, description (String), quantity (int), unitPrice and lineAmount (BigDecimal). lineAmount is a plain stored field, not computed. No back-reference to SalesOrder, so equals/hashCode/toString cannot recurse. No-arg and all-fields constructors, getters/setters, equals/hashCode/toString.
symbols: SalesOrderLine(long, String, String, int, BigDecimal, BigDecimal)

changes.description: Public parent POJO in package com.neversoft.sales. Private fields id (long), orderDate (LocalDate), status (String), customer (Customer), lines (List<SalesOrderLine>, initialised to an empty ArrayList, never null). No-arg and all-fields constructors. setCustomer associates a Customer. getLines returns an unmodifiable view; setLines copies the input (null -> empty); addLine rejects null with NPE; removeLine returns boolean. equals/hashCode/toString cover all five fields; no recursion because children and customer hold no reference to SalesOrder.

Dependency-free test harness in the style of VehicleTest.java (main, test, check, eq helpers, exit 1 on failure) covering all three classes. Javadoc gives the javac --release 25 -Xlint:all -Werror and java run commands. Not wired into package.json, to keep AC-7.

interfaces.notes: Package com.neversoft.sales. getLines is an unmodifiable view and never null; setLines and the constructor copy the input list; addLine(null) throws NullPointerException.

test_approach.what: Compile the three main classes and SalesOrderLine/SalesOrder/Customer test with javac --release 25 -Xlint:all -Werror using only the JDK (no classpath); expect no warnings or errors, then run SalesOrderTest and expect exit 0.
git status / git diff --name-only shows only new files under src/main/java/com/neversoft/{sales,customer}, src/test/java/com/neversoft/sales and docs/bob/4; no existing file is modified.
Given a Customer, two SalesOrderLines and a new SalesOrder, when the customer is set and both lines added, then getCustomer returns it and getLines holds both lines in insertion order.
Given an order with two lines, when one line is removed, removeLine returns true and one line remains; removing an absent line returns false.
Given objects built with the all-fields constructors, every getter on all three classes returns the value passed in.

Object graph SalesOrder -> Customer + SalesOrderLines: identical graphs are equal with equal hashCode; changing one customer or line field makes them unequal; toString terminates and contains the customer name and each line's item code.

getLines() is unmodifiable (add throws UnsupportedOperationException); addLine(null) throws NullPointerException; mutating the list passed to setLines/constructor afterwards does not affect the order; setLines(null) and the no-arg constructor give an empty non-null list.

Reflection per class: public, superclass Object, no interfaces, declared fields with specified names/types (SalesOrder 5, SalesOrderLine 6, Customer 4), all private and non-static, public no-arg constructor; SalesOrderLine has no field of type SalesOrder.
No-arg defaults (numbers 0, references null, SalesOrder lines empty) and setter/getter round trip per field including null for reference fields.

equals contract (reflexive, symmetric, false for null/other type), equals false when any single field differs per class, hashCode consistent with equals, null-safe equals/hashCode/toString on default instances.
toString of each class contains every field value.

rollout: Purely additive. Order: create Customer.java, SalesOrderLine.java, SalesOrder.java (depends on both), then SalesOrderTest.java; run the javac/java commands from its Javadoc; confirm git status shows only new files. No feature flags. package.json is not touched, so merge order relative to #3 does not matter.
